 KC Bokadia recalls Rajesh Khanna’s loneliness and regret later 
 By
 TNM (With ANI Inputs) 
 ✓
 4 November 2026, 12:52 pm 
 3 min read
 4 Nov 2026 
 ANI Photo | KC Bokadia recalls Rajesh Khanna’s loneliness and regret later 
 Veteran filmmaker KC Bokadia has spoken about the challenging final years of legendary actor Rajesh Khanna, highlighting the superstar’s struggles with loneliness and limited work opportunities in the later part of his career.
 Bokadia described Khanna as a strong individual who suffered emotionally, recalling the actor’s own admission of regret for having ignored film producers earlier in his career. Reflecting on Khanna’s words, Bokadia said, “He was a lion of a man, yet he was suffering. He said this is entirely my own fault—I ignored the producers. Now, I am paying the price.”

 The filmmaker also addressed the isolation Khanna experienced as his films stopped performing well at the box office. He recounted that producers who had eagerly sought to work with Khanna gradually stopped visiting his office on Linking Road in Mumbai. “No one used to come in the last stage. He used to stand all day. There was his office on Linking Road. He used to smoke all day. No one used to come. People used to say that. We saw it too. Because the films flopped. Plus they used to say that it was very painful for him; no producers used to come to him,” Bokadia said.
 Regarding the industry’s changing attitude towards actors depending on the success of their films, Bokadia acknowledged, “It happens like this. This is how it is. There are only a few good people.”
 ADVERTISEMENT 
 Amid these difficult recollections, Bokadia shared a personal memory that revealed Khanna’s warmth and hospitality. He recalled being respectfully invited to dinner by Khanna, who was fond of cooking, particularly ‘kadhi and gatte ki sabzi.’ “He invited me to eat, and he called me so respectfully. And he said, Mr Bokadia, look, I have made kadhi and gatte ki sabzi for you,” Bokadia recalled.
 Bokadia described Khanna as someone who enjoyed food and hosting grand parties, although the filmmaker noted he never attended those gatherings.
 When asked why Khanna’s films eventually stopped succeeding, especially as Amitabh Bachchan’s ‘Angry Young Man’ image gained prominence and romantic films lost appeal, Bokadia attributed it to fate. “It’s all a game of fate,” he said.
 ADVERTISEMENT 
 Drawing on his own experience in filmmaking, Bokadia explained that predicting an actor’s success was not an exact science. He recalled working with established stars and identifying actors who later became superstars. He also mentioned an incident involving veteran actor Rajkumar expressing disbelief at how some actors achieved stardom.
 Bokadia further spoke about his association with Amitabh Bachchan, recalling how the actor signed the film ‘Aaj Ka Arjun’ without hearing the story.
 KC Bokadia collaborated with Rajesh Khanna on three notable films. He produced ‘Main Tera Dushman’ (1989) and co-produced ‘Paap Ka Ant’ (1989), both featuring Khanna in special appearances. Their most prominent collaboration was ‘Pyaar Zindagi Hai’ (2001), produced by Bokadia, in which Khanna played Hridaynath, a loving father protecting his daughters.
